title: Tech selloff drags the market lower on Friday
summary: US stocks fell on Friday as big technology companies kept sliding. The S&P 500 lost about 1.1% and the Nasdaq about 2%, and chip makers were hit hard as worries grew about how long the AI building boom can last. The Nasdaq ended the week down roughly 4.5%, its worst week since late June.
why: When investors get nervous about one hot idea, like AI chips, many stocks tied to it fall together. That is why owning companies from different industries can make the ride smoother. A bad day or week is common and does not say what happens next.

title: Long term US government bond yield stays near 5.1%
summary: The yield on the 10 year Treasury was reported near 5.1% on Friday, slightly lower on the day. Our own monthly data show the September average at 4.99%, up from 4.06% a year earlier.
why: A bond yield is the interest the government pays you for lending it money. When safe bonds pay more, stocks have to look more attractive to compete, so high yields can push share prices down, especially for fast growing tech companies.

title: Core inflation comes in hotter than expected
summary: The latest US consumer price report showed core inflation, which leaves out food and energy, rising faster than analysts expected. Coverage says this raises the chance that the Federal Reserve raises interest rates again at its meeting at the end of October.
why: Inflation means prices keep rising. To cool it, the Fed can raise interest rates, which makes borrowing more expensive and can slow companies down. Markets often drop when rate hikes look more likely.

title: Lockheed Martin will report quarterly results on October 22
summary: The company announced it will publish its third quarter results before the market opens on Thursday, October 22, with a webcast at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time. Its stock rose 3.7% on Friday ahead of the report.
why: An earnings report shows how much a company really sold and earned. Stocks often move a lot on report day, up or down, depending on whether results beat what analysts expected.
